judged_text: [Medium/bug] The lenient schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse is selected purely from env vars rather than whether the sync path was actually taken: with sync enabled, responses obtained directly from providers are also minimally parsed and stripped — e.g. salesforce CalendarService persists a stripped Salesforce token (losing instance_url, signature, etc. that jsforce needs), and team credentials (userId null → local refresh) are corrupted the same way.

record.issue_text: [Medium/bug] The lenient schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse is selected purely from env vars rather than whether the sync path was actually taken: with sync enabled, responses obtained directly from providers are also minimally parsed and stripped — e.g. salesforce CalendarService persists a stripped Salesforce token (losing instance_url, signature, etc. that jsforce needs), and team credentials (userId null → local refresh) are corrupted the same way.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the choice of schema is based only on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, not on whether `refreshOAuthTokens` actually used the sync endpoint. This means that when those env vars are set, *all* refresh responses (including direct provider refreshes taken when `userId` is null/absent, e.g. team credentials) are validated/parsed with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of the provider-specific schema passed in. Since Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, this can drop provider-required fields. The diff shows Salesforce now persists refreshed tokens via `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)` and then updates `credential.key` from `accessTokenParsed.data`; with envs set, the minimal schema would be used and could omit fields like `instance_url`/`signature` that `jsforce.Connection` typically relies on, matching the finding’s data-loss/corruption concern.
